thread:
Alex Kim: incident-bot just fired a page for prod-alb-us-east-1 — lots of TLS handshake failures and a bunch of LB targets marked unhealthy. PagerDuty alert ID: PD-98765. Seeing initial spike ~10:03 UTC.
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired -> PD-98765, level: P1. Notifying on-call.
Alex Kim: copying logs: `ALB: TLSHandshakeError: 524 connections failed`, `targetHealth: 38/120 healthy`
Maria Vasquez: I can see increased 5xx for a subset of customers in us-east (metrics dashboard). Customer impact: ~4-6% requests with 503/524.
June Park: confirming — our synthetic checks from us-east-1 show TLS handshake timeout 1-2s then reset.
Sam O'Neill: tagging @Tariq for infra. Any recent cert rotations?
Tariq Singh: not on certs, nothing rotated. Running dig and curl now.
Tariq Singh: `dig +short prod.example.redwood-inference.com` -> returns both us-east and eu-west A records; TTL 300. DNS looks fine.
Tariq Singh: `curl -v https://prod.example.redwood-inference.com/health` -> TLS handshake failure: "alert handshake_failure" from ALB. Dumping ALB target health and backend logs.
Alex Kim: might be backend process crash or socket limit. Sam, can you check target instance logs?
Sam O'Neill: pulling /var/log/nginx/error.log on targets i-0a... shows `TLS: no shared cipher` on some workers. Looks like mismatched cipher negotiation for a subset of targets (maybe kernel/OpenSSL change?).
June Park: any recent AMI/OS patch deploys on those hosts?
Tariq Singh: we pushed a glibc/OpenSSL patch in a small rolling update to the dedicated pool last night to 6 hosts. Could be related. Rolling back patch on those hosts now.
pagerduty-bot: PD-98765 acknowledged by Alex Kim at 10:07 UTC. Escalation paused.
Alex Kim: good. Initiating immediate failover: update ALB target-group weights to shift 80% traffic to healthy eu-west pool, keep 20% to us-east for diagnostics. Applying target-group weights now.
Tariq Singh: starting rollback of the patch on the 6 affected instances (i-0a..., i-0b...). Also putting affected targets OutOfService in the target group so ALB stops routing to them.
Maria Vasquez: notify CS — potential user sessions in us-east might see errors. Sending one-line to #support.
June Park: running `sudo systemctl restart nginx` on remaining us-east nodes to flush states.
Sam O'Neill: confirming NGINX restarts succeeded. Health checks returning 200 on remaining nodes.
Alex Kim: telemetry after failover: error rate dropped from 5.2% -> 0.6% over 4 minutes. TLS handshake failures decreased immediately.
Tariq Singh: rollback done on 6 hosts; re-running openssl s_client checks. `openssl s_client -connect i-0a...:443` -> now completes handshake, ciphers TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 negotiated. Good. Marking targets back InService one by one.
incident-bot: Target group update applied, traffic weights modified.
pagerduty-bot: PD-98765 status -> acknowledged; awaiting monitor OK before resolving.
Maria Vasquez: CS updated customers in affected cohort with incident note and status. No immediate SLA breach expected; working on a short incident report.
June Park: root cause appears to be a regressed OpenSSL patch that removed/changed preferred ciphers on certain AMI builds; caused cipher negotiation failures on older kernel/openssl combos.
Sam O'Neill: next steps: audit AMI builds for cipher defaults, add pre-rollout TLS negotiation smoke tests, and add ALB routing auto-shift policy for TLS target health spike.
Alex Kim: agreed. Action items: 1) Postmortem (owner: June) due EOD tomorrow. 2) AMI/patch audit (owner: Tariq) high priority. 3) Add smoke tests to deploy pipeline (owner: Sam). 4) Customer follow-up (owner: Maria).
Tariq Singh: I'll also add an automated alert that correlates TLS handshake errors with recent package deployments.
Alex Kim: any objections to closing the page once PD auto-monitors go green for 15m?
pagerduty-bot: PD-98765 will auto-resolve when monitors are healthy for 15 minutes.
June Park: no objections.
Alex Kim: thanks team — excellent quick work. If anything regresses ping this thread. Closing actions in ops board now. :thumbsup:
Maria Vasquez: adding incident label and tag for DNS/ALB/TLS in docs.
June Park: will write the timeline.
Tariq Singh: will also spin up a canary deploy with the reverted package and run through TLS matrix.
Sam O'Neill: leaving a note in runbook about this cipher regression scenario.
Alex Kim: incident closed for now — moving to follow-up.
